clue.text: He had a brother in Paris

definitions.text: He had a brother in Paris

parts.words: He had a brother in Paris
parts.note: reads like a man with a sibling living in the French capital, but Paris is the Trojan prince whose elder brother was the hero of Troy

explanation.surface: Someone recalls a man whose brother lived in the French capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Paris looks like the city; it is the Trojan prince who carried off Helen, and his brother was Troy's champion in the Iliad.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek legend the Trojan champion slain by Achilles was a son of Priam and so a brother of the prince Paris.

clue.text: Historian or Judaean ruler ? Up to us!

parts.note: Herod was the king of Judaea at the time of the Nativity

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the next word is written from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written before turning
taken as written

explanation.surface: A quiz asks whether a figure was a historian or a Judaean king, leaving the choice to us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up' turns TO into OT, which sits between HEROD and US; 'or' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek writer of the Histories is called the father of history.

clue.text: Provide food to an old robber

parts.note: to cater is to supply food and drink
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is told to feed an elderly thief.
explanation.walkthrough: A cateran was a Highland marauder, a Scottish word now old-fashioned.
explanation.definitionFit: Cateran is an old Scots word for a raiding brigand of the Highlands.

parts.note: dramatic suggests a thriller film, but here it means at the theatre: a small binocular brings the stage near

explanation.surface: A camera technique gives a film its tense close-up shots.
explanation.definitionFit: Small binoculars used in a theatre bring the performers on stage visually closer.

definitions.meaning: to hold out stubbornly against pressure
as a verb, to jut or protrude

explanation.surface: Keep holding out against a scheme you dislike.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both persisting in resistance and protruding from a surface.

clue.text: Will try to have last word on Tuesday opening

parts.note: to try something is to test it
amen is the word that closes a prayer

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, here taken from Tuesday

explanation.surface: Someone attempts to have the final say when Tuesday begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening' takes the first letter of Tuesday, T, to end the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal document stating how someone's property is to be passed on after death.

definitions.meaning: the sailors who work a vessel
the old past tense of crow, as in the cock crowed, meaning boasted or cheered loudly

explanation.surface: The sailors cheered at the top of their voices.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is the archaic past tense of 'crow' ('the cock crew'), a crowing being loud exultation.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the body of sailors aboard and the old past tense of a verb meaning to cheer triumphantly.

clue.text: See alumnus make a hit in court

parts.note: OB is old boy, a former pupil
in tennis a serve is the stroke that starts a point on court

explanation.surface: A former student watches someone strike a winning blow at a legal hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court' suggests law; it is a tennis court. OB (old boy) is British for a former pupil of a school.
explanation.definitionFit: To watch or notice something is to see it.

clue.text: Can turn for example into the shade

parts.note: a tin is a can for food

indicators.note: turn tells us the abbreviation for 'for example' is flipped round

explanation.surface: A can goes into the shadows as an illustration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' makes EG into GE, which follows TIN; 'into' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A slight trace of colour is a shade or hint.

indicators.note: the answer arrives inside the words that follow, spread across them

explanation.surface: A creature finishes ahead of the field once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes in' hides the answer across 'firST AGain'.
explanation.definitionFit: A male deer is an animal.

clue.text: Might be beaten by the losers ?

definitions.text: Might be beaten by the losers ?

parts.words: Might be beaten by the losers ?
parts.note: sounds like a team that could suffer defeat at the hands of the weaker side, but an army that is losing beats a withdrawal

explanation.surface: A strong side might be defeated by underdogs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beaten' looks like defeated; the idiom is to beat a hasty withdrawal, which losing armies do.
explanation.definitionFit: A falling back of troops is what a defeated army beats, in the idiom.

clue.text: Relative by marriage makes stage appearance ?

definitions.meaning: a spouse's son from an earlier relationship
an actor walks onto the stage, read as two words

explanation.surface: An in-law turns up in the theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: Split into two words, the answer describes an actor walking onto the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A wife's or husband's son by a previous partner is a relation acquired through marriage, and walking onto a stage is stepping on.

clue.text: Was his picture thought worthy of an Oscar ?

definitions.text: Was his picture thought worthy of an Oscar ?

parts.words: Was his picture thought worthy of an Oscar ?
parts.note: reads as film awards, but the Oscar is Wilde, whose novel centres on a portrait that ages in its sitter's place

explanation.surface: A film critic wonders whether a movie deserved an Academy Award.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picture' and 'Oscar' suggest films; they are the portrait in Oscar Wilde's novel and Wilde himself.
explanation.definitionFit: Wilde's novel is about a young man whose portrait ages while he stays youthful.

parts.note: reads as a stiff performer of the past, but means something made of wood that is also the surname of Herbert Beerbohm, a Victorian actor-manager

explanation.surface: An elderly performer delivers his lines stiffly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wooden' looks like a criticism of acting; Herbert Beerbohm Tree was a famous Victorian-Edwardian actor-manager, and a tree is made of wood.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Herbert Beerbohm of that surname was a leading London actor-manager, and the plant itself is all timber.

clue.text: Satisfied to let off a few being high-spirited

parts.note: to satisfy a demand is to meet it, so satisfied gives met

indicators.note: off signals that the letters of let go wrong and are rearranged

parts.note: some means a small number

explanation.surface: Someone is content to release a handful of lively animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges LET into TLE, between MET and SOME; 'being' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Full of spirit and courage, as a lively horse is spirited and eager.

parts.note: tan is a light brown colour

indicators.note: breaks shows the letters of legs smashed up and reset

explanation.surface: Someone named Brown fractures limbs, causing complications.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaks' rearranges LEGS into GLES after TAN; 'result' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Knots and muddles are complications.

definitions.meaning: withdrawn from a race or contest before it starts
marked by a light wound from claws or a sharp point

explanation.surface: A cricketer leaves the field injured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired hurt' is a cricket term for a batter leaving injured; split, the words give two meanings of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse withdrawn from a race is struck off, and skin grazed by claws has been lightly wounded.

parts.note: Eve is a girl's name
the rest is what remains

explanation.surface: A girl stays in first position.
explanation.definitionFit: The world's highest mountain is the ultimate summit.

clue.text: Abstainer swallows your gin cocktail for testing

indicators.note: swallows means one piece takes the other inside it

parts.note: TT is teetotal, a person who does not drink alcohol

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A teetotaller downs a gin drink to see what it is like.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cocktail' mixes YOURGIN into RYINGOU, which TT 'swallows'; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Trialling something is putting it through a test.

indicators.note: sound signals a word pronounced the same as the name of the philosopher

parts.note: Herbert Spencer was a Victorian philosopher

explanation.surface: A poet is said to be a reliable thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like 'reliable'; it signals that the poet's name sounds like the philosopher Herbert Spencer's.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmund, author of The Faerie Queene, was an Elizabethan poet.

parts.note: reads as hurtful remarks, but observations here are looks: a glance believed to cast a curse

explanation.surface: A critic makes cruel remarks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'observations' suggests comments; it means looking, and a malevolent stare was believed to cause harm.
explanation.definitionFit: A malicious glance once believed to bring bad luck or injury.

parts.note: a tot is a small child
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: Completely the youngster's companion, in a way.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive gives no letter: the child's friend is TOT plus ALLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Completely or entirely.

clue.text: Wood gets in fish with rope

indicators.note: gets in means the wood is placed inside the fish

parts.note: the ling is a sea fish
ash is a timber

explanation.surface: A timber boat brings in fish with ropes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets in' puts ASH inside LING; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Cord used for tying things down.

parts.note: p is piano, softly, in music
an air is a melody

explanation.surface: A soft melody, or perhaps a duet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A' and 'or' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A couple of matching things.

indicators.note: say signals a word heard rather than spelt

parts.note: peace is quiet, calm

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a little quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: A portion or fragment of something.

indicators.note: embraces means holding the other piece inside

parts.note: the number points to the answer at eleven across, the relative by marriage
a hen is a female bird

explanation.surface: A clue number holds a woman engineer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embraces' puts HEN inside the 11-across answer.
explanation.definitionFit: George, builder of the Rocket locomotive, was a pioneering railway engineer.

definitions.meaning: the ruffe, a small freshwater perch, also has another name
Alexander was a poet of the eighteenth century, and several pontiffs took the name

explanation.surface: A frilly collar chosen for a man named Alexander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruff' looks like a collar; it is the fish ruffe, also called the pope. Alexander Pope was the poet, and several popes were Alexander.
explanation.definitionFit: The ruffe fish has an old alternative name shared with the pontiff, and Alexander was both a poet's first name and a papal title.

clue.text: Very big part for Eva Strong

indicators.note: part signals that the answer is a portion of the following words

explanation.surface: A large role is written for an actress called Eva Strong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part' hides the answer in 'eVA STrong'; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Immense in size.

definitions.meaning: a lotion that cleans the eyes

explanation.surface: Something that makes our outlook clearer about deception.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A lotion for bathing tired eyes, and a slang term for nonsense or deceit.

parts.note: pro means in favour of
VI is six in Roman numerals
so means thus

explanation.surface: A stipulation drawn up for six people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A clause stating a requirement in an agreement.

parts.note: even means level or balanced

indicators.note: possibly shows the letters of diet may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: It is time for a balanced diet, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges DIET into TIDE after EVEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A poetic word for evening, a time of day.

clue.text: Point to a figure of importance

parts.note: W is west, a compass point
eight is a figure

explanation.surface: Indicate someone important.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Point' is a compass point; 'to' and 'of' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Influence or significance, as in an opinion carrying force.
